desc: The Air Force is the origin point of the entire American UFO record and of the entire American denial record. Established as an independent service on 18 September 1947 - eleven weeks after the Roswell press release issued by the 509th Bomb Group at Roswell Army Air Field - it inherited Project SIGN (1948), Project GRUDGE (1949) and Project BLUE BOOK (1952-1969) at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, the same installation that every retrieval account since 1947 identifies as the destination of recovered material. The National Archives records that from 1947 to 1969 'a total of 12,618 sightings were reported to Project BLUE BOOK. Of these 701 remain Unidentified', and that 'On December 17, 1969, the Secretary of the Air Force announced the termination of Project BLUE BOOK', a decision resting on the University of Colorado's 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects' and a National Academy of Sciences review of it; the collection now sits at NARA as 94 rolls of 35mm microfilm, T-1206. The Air Force also produced the two modern Roswell rebuttals - 'The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' (1994) and 'The Roswell Report: Case Closed' (1997) - which attributed the debris to Project MOGUL and the bodies to anthropomorphic test dummies dropped in the 1950s, an explanation that requires the witnesses to have misdated events by up to a decade. Wright-Patterson remains the home of the Air Force Research Laboratory and of the Foreign Technology Division lineage that became the National Air and Space Intelligence Center, and the Air Force retains the largest single share of the Department's special access program portfolio.

dossier.denialPosture: The Air Force's posture is not silence but re-description, and it is the same shape in 1953, 1969 and 1985. In 1953 the regulation permitted public discussion of identified objects and forbade it for unidentified ones, which converts every open case into a non-statement. In 1969 the public collection channel was closed with a scientific justification while the foreign-materiel channel continued under separate authority. In 1985 the service declined to confirm a programme whose figures its own department had already published, on standing orders. In each case the denial is procedural rather than substantive: not 'this did not happen' but 'this is not a thing I am permitted to describe' -- which is why the board grades the Aurora edge as a directed denial with the Air Force named as its issuer, and why nothing here is graded as a denial of anomalous material, which the service has not been documented making in these records.
dossier.narrative:
Everything this board argues about custody runs through one service, and the useful thing a dossier can do is set the public record and the internal record side by side using only documents.

The public record is well known and well sourced. From 1947 to 1969, 12,618 sightings were reported to Project BLUE BOOK, of which 701 remain unidentified; on 17 December 1969 the Secretary of the Air Force announced its termination, resting on the University of Colorado study and a National Academy of Sciences review; the files went to the National Archives as 94 rolls of microfilm, T-1206. Two later reports attributed the Roswell debris to Project MOGUL and the bodies to anthropomorphic test dummies dropped in the 1950s -- an explanation requiring witnesses to have misdated events by up to a decade.

The internal record is the same service, described by its own units. AFR 200-2 of 26 August 1953, signed by order of the Secretary of the Air Force by Nathan Twining, designated ATIC as the analysis authority, directed that 'All evidence will be forwarded to ATIC', instructed units to safeguard materiel against 'defacing or alteration which would reduce its value for technical analysis', and limited public release to objects 'conclusively identified by ATIC as a conventional aerial device'. Fourteen years later, and two years before Blue Book closed, the 1127th USAF Field Activities Group's own semiannual history lists Project BLUE FLY and Project MOON DUST under FOREIGN MATERIEL PROGRAM, records exploitation personnel deployed to crash sites, and describes about three tons of parts airlifted to Wright-Patterson under a Joint Chiefs priority designation. JANAP 146 was still listing unidentified flying objects as a reportable category in 1977.

None of that establishes anomalous material. All of it establishes that the collection channel the public was told had closed was not the only channel, and that the service said so in documents it classified rather than published.
openQuestions: The 1127th USAF Field Activities Group's activation and inactivation dates are not established. No primary lineage record was found, and its Fort Belvoir station appears only in secondary accounts.
The US deorbit figure on page 30 of the 1127th's 1 January - 30 June 1967 history is illegible in the released scan at 340 dpi and is not reported anywhere on this board.

The FY1986 Department of Defense Procurement Programs (P-1) exhibit that carried the Aurora line has not been located or read. Everything on this board about its contents comes from a named Washington Post correspondent reporting them in February 1985.
ATIC's 1947-1951 T-2 intelligence files have never been subject to a comprehensive declassification review.
dossier.whatItIs: The United States Air Force, established as an independent military department on 18 September 1947, eleven weeks after the Roswell press release issued by the 509th Bomb Group at Roswell Army Air Field. It inherited and ran every official American UFO project -- Project SIGN in 1948, Project GRUDGE in 1949 and Project BLUE BOOK from 1952 to 1969 -- at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, the installation every retrieval account since 1947 names as the destination of recovered material.
dossier.whyImplicated: The Air Force is the origin point of both the American UFO record and the American denial record, and it is the only institution on this board that is simultaneously the collector, the analyst, the custodian and the public voice. Under AFR 200-2 it required reports to flow to the Air Technical Intelligence Center -- the foreign-materiel exploitation shop -- and restricted public discussion to cases conclusively identified as conventional. It closed Blue Book publicly in December 1969 while its own units continued to run a Foreign Materiel Program whose 1967 unit history lists MOON DUST and BLUE FLY alongside MIG-17 exploitation and describes airlifting recovered materiel to Wright-Patterson. And in February 1985 an Air Force spokesman, reminded that his own department had published Aurora's figures in an unclassified procurement document, said his orders were still to say only that it was a classified program.
